newsitem.title: USA: Judge deals setback to Orange Cty-related lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Judge deals setback to Orange Cty-related lawsuit.

text.p: A judge told several municipalities that sued Merrill Lynch & Co over Orange County, Calif., investment losses to amend their suit against the brokerage giant, attorneys said Thursday.

Contra Costa County Superior Court Judge Ignazio Ruvolo granted Merrill Lynch's motion to dismiss the suit but gave the localities 20 days to amend their complaint, according to Michael Kahn and Greg Call, attorneys for the municipalities.
They plan to refile the suit on December 2. "We are still confident that we will prevail and proceed," Call said.
Merrill Lynch said it was pleased by the court's decision.
"Merrill Lynch is pleased that the court correctly recognized that these municipalities could not pursue the claim they have raised," a Merrill Lynch spokeswoman said.

The lawsuit was filed by 14 municipalities -- including Atascadero, Mountain View and Santa Barbara -- against Merrill Lynch. The suit alleged that the brokerage firm defrauded the municipalities that had invested in Orange County's ill-fated portfolio, Call said. They are seeking $80 million in damages.
Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing.
Separately, Orange County has filed a $2-billion-plus lawsuit against the firm, alleging it sold the county risky securities in violation of state law.
Merrill Lynch asserts that the county's massive investment losses resulted from the county's "ill-advised" decision to declare bankruptcy.
The county filed for bankruptcy protection Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
